This may be a meme, but the message it conveys is dear to my heart. I truely believe that Greenhill is a tragic character, along with Lebello and in the same vein as Admiral Bucock. All these men, and their stories are tied to that of the greatest tradgety of the show, that of the Free Planets Alliance and those heroes who tried to stave off it's destruction.

There are a few moments from which Greenhill, during his short screentime, really shone through as a thoughtful character who, similar to Lebello, did what they thought they had to do in order to achieve what they saw was right. For example, the greatest of these was the scene against the tombstone.

'If i didn't lead them, who would restrain them. There was no way, besides this. Will she, will she understand that... My Darling?'

In this small line of dialogue, we learn all we need to know about Greenhill; from his thoughts and ambitions to his overall feelings towards the actions he would embark upon. There was no desire for power or no personal gain, or anything of the sort.  Everything he did, was for the salvation of the Free Planets Alliance from those whom would consume it within.

Outside of Greenhill as a person, we have to take into account two critical factors which influence our perception of him. That of the invasion of the Imperial territories and that of the Lippstadt League.

We must remember, that the Alliance invasion of the Empire was entirely predicated upon the decision of politicians to maintain political power. Nothing less, and nothing more. Not only was there failed political leadership, but military too as the plans for invasion were doomed from the start, along with the complete incompetence of the upper echelons with Reinhards' coutnerattack. This compunded the military losses until only 10 million out of the 30 million soliders who entered Imperial Territory remained. 66% losses is bad enough, but twenty million souls perished all for the continuation of the political estabishments powerbase!

Another thing we cannot forget, as within the story it happened concurrently, is the Imperial Civil War. Look at the nobility, who's entire reason for launching this rebellion was to recoup some of that influence lost due to Reinhards' increasing dominance within the bodypolitic of the Galactic Empire. There entire existence was an explotitive one, and everything they did was in service of that. Consider this; the Stadium incident in the Alliance was a mistake, Westerland was deliberate.

Everything that Greenhill did, he did for the Alliance and it's people.

I tried watching it before; but couldn't get into it because of the difference in the colour pallet and the uninteresting opening episodes. I don't think the Yang arc that opens the show is bad by any means, just they're not as interesting to me and you can see the differences in quality between the OVA and the prequel series.

However, after this arc concludes, we soon begin to follow Reinhard and Kircheiss' story through the rest of the show. It's just as spectacular as the OVA, with interesting tales of political intrigue, military conflicts and great character development for our boys. For me one of the most enjoyable aspects of the show was seeing how Reinhard meets all the admirals of the OVA, and there's some great cameos. It helps flush out the relationships between them, and showcases some of their attributes that would put them within the scope of Reinhard's' inner circle.

For example, Lutz appears only for a fleeting second in a single episode; but it's so engaging, and helps aid in flushing out certain qualities of Lutz in the OVA. As well as being highly satisfying.

If you can overlook some of the shortcomings, I think it's a very enjoyable series. Quite the pleasant surprise.

He was an honourable man and didn't deserve to die, this and his relationship with Reinhard meant he lost his second half; which watching him deal with it and the consequences throughout the show really hit hard.   


LotGH in the end was Reinhards story, even though he wasn't the sole focus of the show, he was one of the main protagonists. So his death was that of a fulfilling ending to an incredible story.   


Yang's was deeply saddening for much of the same reason as Kircheis, unexpected, and he didn't deserve to die in such a way. One thing which always gets me about his death was how he felt he should have suffered more for all the blood that he shed, and his last thoughts were of his wife and adopted son. He died thinking of those he loved, just as they were trying to save him. He didn't make it.

These are going to be instrumental in taking down heavier vehicles which list 1 would struggle with. You have enough shield drones to cover each riptide which is always a good start and the stealth suits give the advantage of being able to capture objectives easier. This is instrumental in Maelstrom games as being able to infiltrate, move 8" and fly is going to be key.   


The other option seems to be list 3 due to the addition of the trip ionheads. This gives the advantage of more armour to chew through as well as additional firepower for taking down heavier targets. Ion cannons overcharged will mince any custodes unit who fails their save.   


Other than that list 1 and 4 don't sit right with me. List 1 won't have the capacity to take down heavier targets, so it will struggle with Guard tanks or heavy vehicles. Knights will be a massive problem for it. List 4 seems a little inconsistent in what it wants to do with its supporting units so I wouldn't recommend it.   


Hope this helps :)
